results.title: Measurements of biodiversity
results.content: where [math]n\_i=N p\_i[/math] denotes the abundance of the [math]i[/math]-th species in the sample ([math]\sum\_{i=1}^S n\_i =N[/math] = the total number of individuals in the sample) and [math]\omega\_{ij}[/math] is the 'distinctness weight' given to the path length (usually the number of steps in the dendrogram) linking species [math]i[/math] and [math]j[/math] in the hierarchical classification. Nearly all diversity and evenness indices are based on the relative abundance of species, thus on estimates of [math]p\_i[/math] in which [math]p\_i = n\_i / N [/math], with [math]n\_i[/math] the abundance of the [math]i[/math]-th species in the sample and [math]N = \sum \_{i = 1}^S \, n\_i[/math] with [math]S[/math] the total number of species in the sample. It is assumed that individuals and species are randomly distributed in the sample and that the total number [math]N[/math] of individuals is large. With this definition, a measure of the information entropy in a large sample is given by the logarithm of the number [math]P[/math] of all different permutations of individuals that give the same distribution of individuals over species.

results.content: Migdall, Joint Quantum Institute (United States) High-precision time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC), single-photon and entangled-photon generation, quantum communication, and ultrafast quantum optics demand laser sources that deliver both short pulses and exceptional timing stability. We present the performance and application potential of Menhir Photonics' low-noise femtosecond and picosecond laser system, which combines sub-10 fs timing jitter and repetition rates up to 10 GHz. Operating at telecom-compatible wavelengths (1535 or 1553 nm), this type of lasers are already in used as a compelling solution for scalable and field-deployable quantum technologies. Polyakov, National Institute of Standards and Technology (United States), Univ. Path-entangled single-photon states are an attractive resource for entanglement distribution on quantum networks. Quantum information processing and communication protocols based on time-bin entangled photonic qudits Here, we present two frameworks enabling the generation and manipulation of time-bin entangled photonic qudits for both fundamental and applied quantum information processing.
